text: In this meta-analysis of randomized trials, intermittent fasting significantly reduced body weight and waist circumference compared with baseline diets.
Time-restricted eating produced modest but significant weight loss over 12 weeks in adults with overweight and obesity.
In a randomized controlled trial, 16:8 time-restricted eating did not produce significantly greater weight loss than a standard three-meal schedule and was associated with loss of lean mass.
Intermittent energy restriction was not superior to continuous energy restriction for weight loss at 12 months of follow-up.
This review discusses proposed circadian and metabolic mechanisms by which the timing of meals might influence energy balance and appetite.
Among marathon runners, skiers, and soldiers exposed to heavy physical stress, regular vitamin C supplementation roughly halved the incidence of the common cold.
Regular vitamin C supplementation did not reduce the incidence of colds in the general community, with no significant effect on how often participants became ill.
Regular supplementation modestly reduced the duration of cold symptoms, although the frequency of catching a cold was unchanged.
High-dose icosapent ethyl reduced the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events by about 25 percent among statin-treated patients at high risk.
Supplementation with one gram per day of marine n-3 fatty acids did not significantly reduce major cardiovascular events in the overall trial population.
This systematic review found that omega-3 supplements have little or no effect on cardiovascular mortality or coronary events.
Marine omega-3 fatty acids lower serum triglyceride concentrations through hepatic mechanisms, but this analysis did not assess clinical endpoints.
In an individual participant data meta-analysis, vitamin D supplementation protected against acute respiratory tract infection, with the largest benefit in those who were deficient at baseline.
In a large randomized trial, monthly vitamin D supplementation did not reduce the incidence of acute respiratory infections in the general adult population.
Meta-analysis showed that probiotics improved global irritable bowel syndrome symptoms and abdominal pain compared with placebo.
In this randomized trial, a multi-strain probiotic was no better than placebo for irritable bowel syndrome symptom relief.
The optimal strain, dose, and treatment duration of probiotics for irritable bowel syndrome remain uncertain given substantial heterogeneity between studies.
In a large prospective cohort, higher habitual coffee consumption was associated with lower all-cause mortality over follow-up.
After adjustment for smoking status, the association between coffee intake and mortality was no longer statistically significant.
Because this was an observational study, the findings cannot establish a causal effect of coffee on mortality.

text: In this randomized trial, zinc supplementation had no significant effect on the duration or severity of cold symptoms.
Several manufacturer-funded trials reported that glucosamine sulfate reduced pain scores in knee osteoarthritis.
In a large independent trial, glucosamine was not significantly better than placebo for reducing knee osteoarthritis pain overall.
In a large randomized trial, Ginkgo biloba did not prevent dementia or slow cognitive decline in older adults.
A few small trials suggested modest improvement in memory tests with Ginkgo biloba extract.
In a small randomized trial of older adults with insomnia, magnesium supplementation improved subjective sleep quality and sleep onset.
A systematic review concluded that current evidence for magnesium improving sleep is of low quality and remains inconclusive.
Meta-analysis found that green tea catechins produced a small but significant reduction in body weight and fat.
In this trial, green tea extract did not significantly reduce body fat compared with placebo.
Long-term vitamin E supplementation did not reduce the risk of cardiovascular events and showed no benefit over placebo.
This paper reviews the antioxidant hypothesis and describes the design of ongoing supplementation studies.
Meta-analysis showed that garlic supplementation significantly lowered systolic blood pressure in hypertensive participants.
In normotensive adults, garlic had no significant effect on blood pressure compared with placebo.
Meta-analysis indicated that melatonin modestly reduced the time to fall asleep in people with insomnia.
This overview describes melatonin pharmacokinetics and its role in circadian regulation without testing an insomnia outcome.
High-intensity interval training significantly improved cardiorespiratory fitness compared with moderate continuous exercise.
A low-carbohydrate diet significantly lowered HbA1c at six months compared with a low-fat control diet.
At two years, differences in glycemic control between low-carbohydrate and control diets were no longer statistically significant.
This narrative review summarizes national dietary guidelines and does not evaluate the efficacy of any specific intervention.
This cross-sectional survey characterized dietary supplement use patterns among adults and reported no clinical outcomes.
